reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge — two validation gaps.*

Reviewed `slug-validation` at `e8612a7` against `main` at `9ba0eca`.

1. *High — validation accepts a matching substring, not the whole slug.*  
   `src/validate.js:1–4`: `/[a-z0-9-]+/` accepts anything containing at least one allowed character. Confirmed that `Xhello`, `a/b`, `../admin`, `hello world`, and `"hello\n"` all pass and produce paths. Encoding afterward doesn’t enforce the documented slug rules. Require a whole-string match, including rejection of trailing line terminators.

2. *Medium — reserved slugs aren’t enforced.*  
   `src/route.js:3–5`: `pagePath` only calls `isValidSlug`; nothing calls `isReserved`. All four reserved names (`new`, `edit`, `admin`, `api`) produce page URLs despite the README saying they cannot be used for pages. Wire the reserved-name check into page-path validation.

*Tests:* All 4 existing tests pass, but they miss both defects. Add negative cases for forbidden characters at the beginning, middle, and end—including newlines—and assert that `pagePath` rejects every reserved name.

No code changed; working tree is clean.
